history.content:
Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().
CheckboxInput setting attrs['checked'] to True: ​https://github.com/django/django/blob/master/django/forms/widgets.py#L527

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)

Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. history.content:
Please solve this issue: SplitArrayField with BooleanField always has widgets checked after the first True value.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. Once this occurs every widget initialized after that defaults to checked even though the backing data may be False. This is caused by the CheckboxInput widget's get_context() modifying the attrs dict passed into it. This is the only widget that modifies the attrs dict passed into its get_context().

		(last modified by Peter Andersen)
	 
When providing a SplitArrayField BooleanField with preexisting data, the final_attrs dict is updated to include 'checked': True after the for loop has reached the first True value in the initial data array. The root cause is visible: `final_attrs` is built once outside the loop and passed to every subwidget, while `CheckboxInput.get_context()` mutates the supplied dictionary by adding `checked=True`. I’ll now verify the mutation and inspect `Widget.build_attrs()` plus the full checkbox implementation so the fix preserves IDs and any caller-supplied attributes without changing unrelated widget behavior.

The defect is confirmed in the source: `CheckboxInput.get_context()` mutates the exact `final_attrs` object passed by `SplitArrayWidget`, and that same object is reused on every loop iteration. I’ll create and run a small standalone reproduction before changing production code, checking both the no-`id` and `id` paths because the bug appears in both.

from django.conf import settings

settings.configure(DEBUG=True, SECRET_KEY='repro', USE_I18N=False)

import django
django.setup()

from django import forms
from django.contrib.postgres.forms import SplitArrayWidget


def show(attrs, label):
    widget = SplitArrayWidget(forms.CheckboxInput(), size=4)
    context = widget.get_context('array', [False, True, False, False], attrs=attrs)
    states = [
        bool(subwidget['attrs'].get('checked'))
        for subwidget in context['widget']['subwidgets']
    ]
    print(label, states)


show(None, 'without id:')
show({'id': 'array'}, 'with id:')
EOF
cd /testbed && python /tmp/repro_split_array_checkbox.py"}
